title: Normality of the finite supremum from a normal-fiber cover
statement: Let A be a domain and K its fraction field. Let s be a finite set of A-subalgebras of K all contained in the integral closure of A in K. Suppose for every prime p of A, some C in s has integrally closed localizations at every prime of C contracting to p. Then every prime localization of the supremum S of s is integrally closed. No Noetherian hypothesis, local-approximation hypothesis, or finite-module hypothesis is needed for this algebraic step.

proof.text: Let B be the finite supremum. Finset.sup_le and le_integralClosure_iff_isIntegral show that B is integral over A. Contract q in Spec B to p in Spec A. Choose C in s by hcover and use Finset.le_sup for C contained in B. Contract q along Subalgebra.inclusion to r in Spec C; Ideal.comap_comap shows r lies over p, so C_r is integrally closed.

The anonymous instance for (S : Subalgebra A K) in Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.AsSubring identifies K as a fraction field of each intermediate subalgebra. The fraction-field clause of the localization-normal-domain lemma identifies K as the fraction field of C_r and B_q, using IsFractionRing.isFractionRing_of_isDomain_of_isLocalization and the algebra structures induced by Localization.mapToFractionRing; this fraction-field argument requires no global normality of C or B. If z in K is integral over A, IsIntegral.tower_top makes z integral over C_r. IsIntegrallyClosed.algebraMap_eq_of_integral gives y in C_r mapping to z. IsLocalization.exists_mk'_eq and mk'_spec write y=c/t and show t*z=c for c in C and t outside r.

For x in K integral over B_q, Mathlib IsIntegral.exists_multiple_integral_of_isLocalization clears the monic equation, producing d outside q such that d*x is integral over B. isIntegral_trans makes d*x integral over A. Step 2 gives t outside r such that t*d*x belongs to C, hence to B. The inclusion sends t outside q by the definition r=comap(q). The product of this image with d is outside q, so IsLocalization.mk' with numerator t*d*x and denominator t*d represents x in B_q. IsLocalization.lift_mk'_spec verifies the equality in K. isIntegrallyClosed_iff then proves that B_q is integrally closed.

from.place: algebraic normality transfer for the finite supremum

lean.statement:
theorem finite_normal_cover_sup_normal (A : Type u) (K : Type v)
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (s : Finset (Subalgebra A K))
    (hs : ∀ C ∈ s, C ≤ integralClosure A K)
    (hcover : ∀ (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime], ∃ C ∈ s,
      ∀ (q : Ideal C) [q.IsPrime], Ideal.comap (algebraMap A C) q = p →
        IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime q)) :
    ∀ (q : Ideal (s.sup (fun C : Subalgebra A K => C) : Subalgebra A K)) [q.IsPrime],
      IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime q)
